item.title: China Hot Springs with Kids: Where to Soak This Winter
item.description:
China Hot Springs with Kids: Where to Soak This Winter

Winter is hot-spring season in China, and for families it works in a way first-time visitors rarely expect: the spring water is often piped straight into your room. Instead of queuing for a public bath with a toddler in tow, you can soak in a private pool on your own balcony, then wander down to a garden of shared pools when the kids want to explore. The deals below are all verified on sale now, and they show the three shapes a family hot-spring stay can take — a room with its own pool, a whole villa, or a water town where the hot spring is one part of a bigger day.

item.title: Harbin Ice and Snow World for First-Timers: What to Know Before You Go
item.description:
Harbin Ice and Snow World for First-Timers: What to Know Before You Go

Harbin Ice and Snow World is the closest thing China has to a city built entirely out of ice. Every winter, workers cut blocks from the frozen Songhua River and stack them into full-size buildings, slides, and sculptures, lit from inside so the whole park glows after dark. It is spectacular, it is enormous, and it is very, very cold. If you are going for the first time, a little planning goes a long way.
